newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia fighters harass, rob aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Liberia fighters harass, rob aid workers.

text.p: Faction fighters harassed and robbed 17 aid workers in western Liberia, the U.N. World Food Programme said on Friday.
The incident happened on Thursday as the team returned from Bo in Cape Mount County where it had been investigating health and nutrition near the border with Sierra Leone.

"As we were returning from Bo we were stopped by about 25 armed fighters who seized all our valuables at gunpoint," WFP Project Officer Mustafa Darboe said in a statement. "They took money, watches and some hand-held radios.
The aid workers, from the U.N. and other relief agencies, were travelling in a four-vehicle convoy. The fighters' regional commander later apologised and some valuables were returned.
The statement did not identify the faction involved but the rival Mandingo and Krahn wings of the ULIMO faction have been fighting for control in the area.

"The civilians we spoke to in Bo told us not to send in food unless the West African Peacekeeping Force could be deployed in the area," Darboe said. "The local population is very afraid of being harassed by fighters."

Last month, aid workers discovered hundreds of starving civilians in the western town of Tubmanburg, which had been sealed off for much of the year. Cape Mount County has also been inaccessible for much of 1996.
Liberia's civil war, launched in 1989, flared in the capital Monrovia in April and May, killing hundreds of people.

West African leaders rallied Liberia's rival warlords round yet another peace deal in August. It envisaged disarmament by January and elections by next May and included the threat of individual sanctions against anyone derailing the deal.
The war has killed well over 150,000 people in Liberia, which freed American slaves set up in 1847.
